News.title: Tragic final hours of mum & 2 kids found dead before husband fled the UK to Zimbabwe
News.content:
THE on-the-run businessman was seen with his estranged wife at their daughter’s sports day hours before his family were found dead.

Nothabo Zandile Tshuma, 42, and her daughters Natalie, 15, and Nala, five, were discovered at their £1.3million home in Great Denham, Bedfordshire, on Monday.



Prior to the terrible discovery, friends of the family have reported Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma, 45, was acting like his typical “polite” and “lovely” self.

The day before the sporting event, Andrew Southam, 64, went to the Tshuma home on Carnoustie Drive to service their pool.



He told the Daily Mail that Tshuma seemed in good spirits and was usually a happy family man who was “always smiling”.

He said: “He was looking forward to his daughter’s sports day and praying that the weather would hold out, because previous sports days had been cancelled.”



It’s not yet clear which of his daughters’ sports day he attended.

Both girls attended private schools in the local area, with Natalie at Bedford Girls School, which costs £20,000-a-year, and Nala went to Pilgrims Pre-Preparatory School.



The couple had recently had their upmarket detached four-bedroom, four-bathroom property valued to be put up for sale as they were in the process of divorcing.

But it’s been revealed that Tshuma told friends he couldn’t live without Zandile and did not want to get separated.

One friend who wanted to remain anonymous told the Mail: “They had been having marriage problems for quite a while. Their relationship had broken down and Zandile had had enough.



“She was a great mother and wife and a lot of the problems were down to Mark’s controlling behaviour. She wanted to start a new life with the kids.”

Another friend who claimed to be a friend of his from Zimbabwe wrote on social media: “He was going through a divorce [I] told him to let her go but he couldn’t.”

The senior IT executive, who earned £100,000 as Head of Development and Support at the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales (ICAEW), was last seen at Heathrow airport on Saturday.

CCTV footage shows the British citizen of Zimbabwean heritage boarding a plane believed to be heading for Zimbabwe.

Cops have warned the triple murder suspect “we will find you” and have urged Tshuma to “do the right thing” and hand himself in.



Yesterday evening, Mrs Tshuma’s cousin Michelle Ncube described how the family “had such high dreams” for the girls, as she paid tribute to their mother outside the home.

She said Mrs Tshuma would be remembered “as the loving, most patient, demure, person, that she was”.

“I think if there’s anything that we remember of her, it’s just how affectionate she was,” she told ITV News.

“She was a naturally private person but she had this warmth and this compassion that really drew you in.

“She was motivated to be a successful black woman,” she said, adding that Mrs Tshuma loved gardening and flowers “and she was a precious flower to us”.



Reflecting on the devastation that had been left behind, Ms Ncube admitted that it “didn’t feel real”, and said the two girls were “absolute dreams”.

“They brought such love joy and light into our lives. We had such high dreams for them. They had such joy, and brought such happiness.”

Mrs Ncube added: “What we want is for us to remember that behind all of this was a woman and two beautiful girls.

“It’s left a massive hole in our hearts. Let the police do their jobs.“

In a touching tribute to 15-year-old Natalie, Mrs Gemma Gibson, Headmistress of Bedford Girls’ School, said: “Natalie was a bright and accomplished Year 10 student who was dearly loved.



“She was a talented dancer, musician, and keen sportswoman. She was fun- loving, full of life and had a positive impact on everyone she came into contact with; she will be remembered with warmth and affection.”

And Headteacher Jo Webster, of Pilgrims Pre- Prep School, added of Nala: “Many of our staff had known Nala since she was seven months old and had the privilege of watching her grow.

“Known for her inquisitive and bubbly nature, positivity, and wonderful sense of humour, she was a little ray of sunshine.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Whether wearing one of her favourite colourful hair accessories, making those around her laugh or taking centre stage in our Pre-School Nativity, Nala brought warmth and happiness wherever she went.

“Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Nala’s family, friends, and everyone affected by this heart-breaking loss.”

News.title: Moment horrified passengers are forced to swim ashore after plane ditches in the sea during terrifying emergency landing
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment horrified passengers swim to shore after their plane ditched in the sea in a terrifying emergency landing.

Jawdropping footage shows the frightened passengers in the ocean as they swim to safety.



The panicked passengers can be seen swimming to shore after the Cessna 402B they were flying in crash-landed in the sea off Haiti on Wednesday morning.

Video shows the pair wading through shallow waters to safety at Ibo beach after their ordeal.



One manages to salvage a bag of possessions and bring they to shore.

Their plane can be seen almost completely submerged in the sea.

The two passengers and a pilot escaped the light aircraft after the water landing at around midday.

All three swam to a nearby beach where they were treated by emergency responders.

They all survived and were able reported to be in stable condition.

The plane had taken off from Cap-Haïtien, bound for Port-au-Prince.



But the twin-engine turboprop, operated by ZED Airlines, came down near Lafiteau just north of the Haitian capital.

A spokesperson for Haitian carrier said the lucky survivors were relieved there were “no human losses to regret”.

No details were released about the cause of the crash landing.



A full investigation was launched by aviation authorities and the airline’s technical team.

The plane, built in 1972, is being checked over.

ZED Airlines said passenger and crew safety was its absolute priority.

They added that the incident didn’t claim any lives thanks to the pilot’s expert handling of the aircraft, as well as a swift response on the ground.

It comes after a seaplane crashed into New York’s East river earlier this month, injuring a 75-year-old grandmother.



Alarming footage from inside the cabin showed the Big Apple‘s skyline flash by before a loud thud is heard.

The seaplane rocks dangerously back and forth before coming to a stop.

It was carrying eight passengers and two pilots when it plummeted into the river in a botched landing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Khloe Todd, 16, said it had been her first time in a seaplane and that the incident had left her “traumatised”.

Two people suffered minor injuries, officials said.

News.title: Does lotto winner whose ticket was BINNED by shopkeeper deserve the prize? VOTE NOW
News.content:
POLL OF THE DAY Does lotto winner whose ticket was BINNED by shopkeeper deserve the prize? VOTE NOW

A DEVASTATED mum discovered she had won a whopping £12million on the Lotto – but a shopkeeper binned her ticket.

Kath Main, 46, read in The Sun that the prize pot was left unclaimed, and the winning numbers matched hers.



But her mum had taken the ticket to be checked at a Londis in Abercynon, South Wales, where they said it was not a winner – and the slip was thrown out.

The 46-year-old said she is left “feeling sick all the time” as she waits for National Lottery operator Allwyn to investigate.



They are expected to rule within 30 days whether the prize pot is rightfully hers.

But even if she is successful, rules on lost tickets mean the mum-of-two wouldn’t get the life changing payout until December 3 – in time for Christmas.

Kath, who had played the winning numbers for 20 years, said: “It’s got to be mine, there’s no other way.”

News.title: Talented artist creates amazing artwork using typewriter – but jokes it takes him hours as he ‘can’t touch type’
News.content:
A TALENTED artist has created a series of impressive artworks including a scene from Wimbledon centre court – using just a vintage typewriter.

James Cook, 29, spends weeks at a time producing the amazing drawings using the retro piece of technology.



From his studio in Canning Town, East London., he can type over a million letters and symbols onto the piece of paper to create his masterpieces.

Impressively, he only uses his right index finger as he “can’t touch type”.

James has been using the typewriter for art since he was aged 17 after first working with it during a school art project.



James also owns around 100 typewriters from across the world, including Europe and Asia – almost all of his typewriters were donated to him by fans.

His work mainly consists of cityscapes from around the world including Rome, Paris, and New York City as well as celebrity portraits, including Shakespeare and Tom Hanks.





But most recently James, from Braintree, Essex., spent six weeks producing his latest piece – which he simply titled “Wimbledon 2026″ – and it has now been viewed over 8 million times on social media.

James said: “I fell in love with the typewriter after using it for the school art project.

“It felt like such a unique way to capture the world.

“I feel like other people express that too when commenting on my social media posts – I guess you wouldn’t ever think it was possible.

“I only use my right index finger as I can’t touch type and it also feels the most comfortable.



“I still can’t believe sometimes that it is my job.

“But the Wimbledon piece has taken me to another level as now I have the actual players and legends like Billie Jean King commenting on my work.

“I pinch myself sometimes to make sure it is all real.”

James’s spark for typewriter art was formed as a 17-year-old while at Braintree Sixth Form.



The project was to “create art with technology”, and James decided on the machine after learning about Paul Smith, who is known as the original “Typewriter Artist”.

James said: “I’ll never forget traipsing around the charity shops in my area looking out for one, but we had no luck until an older couple overheard my dad asking the shopkeeper behind the counter.

“They said I could have their 1950 Oliver Courier model for £15, and I went that same afternoon to pick it up.

“When people ask who my inspiration is, it is Paul Smith.

“He is the ‘OG’ as people say, and there is a reason, as his works are groundbreaking.”



James continued producing his typewriter art when he went to study architecture at University College London, which he later got a degree in.

He says his degree has “inspired” a lot of his cityscape work.

Though he also draws on site, his most recent being the New York City skyline he drew from the Top of the Rock, in New York.



He has also done the Royal Albert Hall and The Ritz.

James then started posting about it on social media as well, leading him to land some commissions.

But his big break came after his work was shown on the BBC News, leading him to be able to become an artist full-time.

He says small A4 artworks can take around five days with larger A3 pieces taking weeks at a time.

Prints range from £96 to £300+ depending on the size.



His most used key is the ‘@’ symbol which he says allows him to create “shading” on his artwork.

For his most recent piece of the Wimbledon Championships he began on Sunday, May 26, and only finished over six weeks later on Friday, June 26.

He says it took him around 378 hours, working around 9 hours almost every day, typing with his right index finger.

He had to feed the piece of paper through the retro machine 20 times and typed over a million times on his 1932 Smith Premier typewriter to produce the extraordinary drawing.

The skilled artist says he loves tennis and decided on the project after seeing adverts on TV for the competition.



He said: “I have always wanted to go to Wimbledon but have never managed to get tickets.

“So I decided I wanted to capture the competition in my own artistic way.”

The artwork shows a game on centre court between heavyweights Novak Djokovic and Roger Federer but is riddled with fun characters and phrases.

These include a ball boy picking up balls, but the bag has ripped, and a man dressed up as a giant strawberry.

James said: “My favourite is the woman who climbed up a ladder and is trying to sneak a peek of the game because they couldn’t get a ticket.”



The artist said he developed this light-hearted style after being inspired by the Where’s Wally puzzle books as a kid.

Inside, he has also included names of players like Andy Murray, Venus Williams, and Sue Barker alongside tennis jargon like “deuce” and “rally”.

He added the green colour of the grass using specially made inked typewriter ribbons.

James said: “A lot of people ask me about how I manage to add colour.

“Most people don’t realise, but a typewriter prints using a ribbon which is pressed against the paper when the letter is pressed.

“There is a person online selling specially made coloured ribbons which have allowed me to add colour to pieces – which has opened up a brand new creative doorway really.



“The green grass really makes the drawing pop and stand out from the black ink, and if anything makes the piece.

“I am immensely proud of it.”

Notable symbols include the use of commas and quotation marks to create texture on the grass and a capital letter ‘G’ for people’s hands.

James says this artwork is the “hardest” he has completed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

This is because he also made a working animation for it which he says took around two weeks to create.



If you would like to see more of James’s work, you can visit his website jamescookartwork.com or Instagram @jamescookartwork Wimbledon is running from June 22 until July 12.

News.title: Museum spreads 800lbs of peanut butter – enough for 15,000 sandwiches – on the FLOOR in bizarre tribute to late artist
News.content:
A NUTTY tribute has been smeared across a museum floor in memory of a beloved late Dutch artist.

More than 800 pounds of peanut butter, enough for around 15,000 sandwiches, has been spread across the floor of a museum in the Netherlands in tribute to Dutch artist Wim T. Schippers, who died last month.



The conceptual artist passed away at the age of 83 and was known for his absurdist and silly works that challenged conventional ideas about the meaning of art.

The peanut butter installation, titled the Pindakaasvloer or peanut butter floor, was first created in 1969.



Now to mark the artists death the piece has been recreated at the Depot offshoot of Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, in Rotterdam.

In 1997, when the peanut butter floor was on display for the second time, Schippers said: Isn’t it fantastic that we are all standing here looking at peanut butter?”



Schippers created the work as part of a Floor Covering Series, which also saw floors covered with glass shards and salt.

The aroma is famously what lingers with many who experience the work first hand.



Museum staff directed visitors for the opening to follow the smell which was wafting by the ticket counter, three floors below where the artwork is laid out.

The conceptual art piece comes with a stark warning – those with a peanut allergy should enter at their own risk.

It took employees working on the latest edition several days to spread 40 buckets of peanut butter across a 270-square-ft hexagon.



Leon Duenk, one of the two men who installed the artwork, said: “It was a lot of work.”

The pair used drywall trowels to smear the peanut butter to a thickness of 2 centimetres.

Prior to his death, the museum and Schippers left instructions on how to recreate the work in the future.

He produced a meticulous 20-point plan that included the requirement to apply the peanut butter as smoothly and boringly as possible and that no one is supposed to stand in or lie down on the peanut butter.

Schippers did not specify the size or shape of the work, but he did say it must to be smooth peanut butter – his preferred brand being that of the Dutch brand Calv.



Calv donated 40 tubs of peanut butter for the latest work.

In 1997, the work was vandalized when a group of people placed 12 slices of bread and several bags of chocolate sprinkles commonly eaten on bread at breakfast in the Netherlands on the floor.

Schippers said: “It doesn’t look bad.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The sprinkles have been applied with a sense of proportion and a skillful hand.”

The installation, which opened on July 10, is scheduled for a two-month run.

News.title: Hosepipe ban loopholes mean you can still wash your dog and fill up your pond – as new rule announced for millions
News.content:
CERTAIN hosepipe ban loopholes mean you can still wash your dog and fill up your pond despite restrictions.

This comes as nearly seven million Brits are set to come under new regulations from the early hours of tomorrow morning.



As Anglian Water announces a new hosepipe ban to households across the East of England, many will still be able to look after pets and fish with a simple work-around for the ban.

Under a hosepipe ban, given the high demand for drinking water, residents cannot use hosepipes, sprinklers or pressure washers to water gardens, clean cars, or fill up swimming pools and hot tubs.



Breaking these rules, when caught, can see homeowners slammed with a £1,000 fine, which is enforced by the water company.

However, the ban does not limit essential uses, especially when it involves the health and safety of people, and general animal welfare.

This means hosepipes can be used for maintaining pet hygiene and washing pets, as well as keeping animals cool during extreme heat.

A hose can also be used to clean out pens and stables to prevent disease, and to fill up drinking water.

For standard care, such as cleaning dogs, water companies suggest using a bucket and sponges instead of a hosepipe, unless a vet confirms your pet has a specific condition that requires a hose to be used.

Similarly, if you have a pool or pond with any fish or aquatic life living in it, a hosepipe can be used to make sure it stays topped up.



This rule is the same for ornamental foundations if they help oxygenate a fish pond, but is not the case if it is purely decorative.

Other hosepipe ban exemptions also mean you can get your car professionally cleaned at a car wash, water newly-laid turf for a month after it was installed, and get patios and paths cleaned by a business.

Despite these loopholes, it is important to remember that a hosepipe ban is implemented to prevent drought conditions and water shortage, so sparing use of any water supply is necessary.

New Anglian Water restrictions are set to begin tomorrow morning at 1am, but customers impacted have been encouraged to “live within the spirit of these restrictions immediately”.

News.title: ‘Cannibal’ mum’s family break silence & make tragic admission after she ‘killed & cooked son, 4’ as shock texts revealed
News.content:
THE family of an alleged cannibal mum admit that they should have “stepped in” before her four-year-old son was discovered murdered.

The brother of the suspected killer revealed his last texts with his sister, just days before she was accused of cooking and eating parts of her son’s arm in Australia.



The young boy was discovered dead with “significant arm injuries” in his home in Wyong.

The tragedy has rocked the reportedly close-knit family of the suspected killer – with her brother saying that his agonised father and older brother are wondering whether they “could have stepped in”.



He told the Daily Mail: “They thought maybe they should have done something more.”

The family also blamed social services of failing the child.



The brother said: “My dad and brother didn’t think [her son] should have been given back to her after she last got out of rehab”.

Her family had previously thrown her out of the home for an alleged drug addiction and her own mother had taken out a court order to protect herself from her daughter’s abuse.

Five months ago, drug counsellors and welfare officers moved the pair to a housing complex in Wyong – where the boy was discovered dead on Saturday.

“We should have been closer to her, I guess”, said her brother.



“And we should have gone and helped her, but this is nothing we could have expected”, he added.

Police raced to the home on Saturday after the woman handed herself in and reportedly confessed to cannibalising her own child.

The mother was arrested on Sunday morning and charged with murder.



The devastating news came as a shock to the family with her brother stating that she seemed “okay” over text.

He said: “I spoke with her days ago, last week, by text. She seemed okay, just usual stuff.

“She was proud of me, what I’ve done… because I had problems too, with my kids.”

He had last seen her three months ago at their mother’s house in Sydney.

He described his little sister as having been a “lovely” girl growing up but having problems as she got older.



When asked how the family was coping with the charges, her shook his and said “we don’t know how this happened”.

Social services had been in contact with the mother and her son three times over suspected neglect and drug abuse.

But the child was still allowed to live with his convicted criminal mother.

New South Wales minister for families and communities Kate Washington revealed on Monday that the last encounter had been 18 months ago.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She also announced that an investigation would be launched to probe into “what decisions were made” and whether they were “adequate”.

News.title: UK’s third heatwave to peak TODAY with Met Office forecasting mercury could hit 36C
News.content:
THE UK’s third heatwave of the year could reach highs of 36C today as another weekend of sun arrives.

Brits are flooding to beaches today as swathes of the country will bask in temperatures of over 30C.



The extensive sunshine and dry weather is set to last for the rest of the week but temperatures will slightly ease in the south and east of England after today’s high.

The southwest will stay warm into next week and the region will see the highest temperatures.



However, today the hottest area will be the Midlands as The Met Office forecasts Birmingham will hit 35C this afternoon, with potential for 36C.

Swathes of the country have been issued with amber and yellow heat health alerts as the heatwave continues.



Met Office Deputy Chief Forecaster Tom Crabtree said: “Many people will understandably want to know how long the current heatwave is likely to last.

“While temperatures are expected to ease across southeast England through the weekend and into next week, it won’t be a straightforward end to the warm weather.

“High pressure is expected to remain in charge through much of next week, but it will gradually migrate northwards.

“This means that an easterly wind will become established in the south, and the focus for the hottest conditions will migrate towards the southwest.

“As a result, some places that have seen the highest temperatures during recent weeks will begin to cool.



“It will however, remain very warm – especially in the southwest – and heatwave thresholds may continue to be met in places.

“The overall signal is for continued fine, dry and very warm weather at times for many parts of the UK into next week. There is however a chance of thunderstorms spreading into parts of the south and southwest.”

Over the weekend, Saturday will is expected to reach 34C before a slight drop to 33C on Sunday.



For Scotland and Northern Ireland temperatures will hit the high 20s today before dipping to the mid 20s on Saturday.

This heatwave will be the longest klasting of the year so far, and could even reach the 1976 record.

The May Bank Holiday heatwave lasted nine days while the record-breaking June heat was a week long.

Humidity levels are forecast to stay lower meaning cooler nights for most areas although cities will likely keep warm overnight.

The heat brings a slight risk of thunderstorms today, especially for western England, but high pressure should keep the country dry.



“A few simple actions can make a huge difference and help prevent fires before they start.”

Forecasters say the temperature gauge will slowly drop as the warm weather eases into the northwest with temperatures staying in the mid-to-high 20s for a prolonged period.

Sun seekers should wear sun protection and keep hydrated as temperatures soar.

The Met Office has also urged anyone hoping to cool off to beware of cold water shock following last month’s deaths.

News.title: Woman in Wimbledon crowd catches cameras' attention due to what's on her head
News.content:
Woman in Wimbledon crowd catches cameras' attention due to what's on her head

A woman in the Wimbledon crowd this week has been praised as 'iconic' after she was caught on camera due to the impressive headpiece she was wearing

View 2 Images The tennis fan caught the attention of the cameras thanks to her headgear (stock photo) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

One woman at Wimbledon has completely stolen the show with her impressive headgear. Thousands of tennis fans have been flocking to London over the past couple of weeks for the annual Wimbledon Championships, and while the tournament is set to come to an end on Sunday (July 12), sports fans are still making the most out of the few days of tennis they have left to enjoy.

‌



And while watching the sport itself should be the main attraction, one woman has gone viral online after she caught the attention of the cameras. A video shared by the official Wimbledon account on TikTok showed a member of the crowd who was dressed in a red and white gingham-patterned top and white sunglasses.

‌



But it was her hat that took people by surprise and made her a viral sensation, with many calling her "iconic". The anonymous woman wore a hat with a magnificent rendition of a Wimbledon tennis court on top of it.

‌



The hat featured a grass court, a net, tennis rackets, and tennis balls. To top it all off, she had even managed to stick a doll to the hat to act as a tennis player, as well as glue a racket onto the doll's hand.

The Wimbledon account wrote alongside the video: "When at Wimbledon!"

View 2 Images The woman went viral after pictures of her hat were shared online (Image: Amer Ghazzal/Shutterstock)

‌



Commenters on the video were in awe of the woman, with many hailing her an "icon" and saying she was "real" for allowing her creativity to flow and completely steal attention from the tennis matches at hand.

One person said: "I love a whimsical girlie."

Another added: "She's so real."

‌



A third simply wrote: "Iconic."

Meanwhile, another Wimbledon attendee was recently left feeling disappointed after he tried the iconic strawberries and cream at the venue for the first time - and it wasn't what he expected.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Lawrence Newport posted a picture on X that showed the inside of a cardboard box, which contained a thin layer of cream at the bottom and what appeared to be a total of seven strawberries haphazardly thrown in.

He wrote alongside the image: "Strawberries and cream at Wimbledon. Not quite as imagined."

Someone else replied directly to Lawrence, stating they didn't know what he expected when "it is literally strawberries and cream". And he hit back to explain that while he did receive what he asked for, it still wasn't what he expected.

Article continues below

He said: "Good point. When I next order fish and chips with tartare sauce, I'll expect a flake of fish, three chips, and tartare sauce just randomly tumbled around it. Oh, and it should all come in a tub that is far too deep, for no reason."

News.title: 'Unacceptable that victims left in the dark' warning over early prison releases
News.content:
'Unacceptable that victims left in the dark' warning over early prison releases

EXCLUSIVE: Ministers face calls to extend existing rules so that victims of all types of crime have the option to find out whether the person who wronged them is being released early

View 2 Images Ministers face calls to make it easier for victims to find out if their offender is being released early (Image: Allan Milligan)

Every victim should be able to find out if the perpetrator of a crime against them is being released early, a charity has demanded.

‌



The head of Victims' Support told The Mirror she is alarmed that only a fraction of those affected by the early release scheme will be able to find out. Ministers have faced a backlash after sex abuse survivors received letters telling them their attacker would be freed earlier than originally expected.

‌



Katie Kempen, Chief Executive of Victim Support, said people affected by other types of crime are in the dark about the person who wronged them being released. She said: “Victims and survivors must not be an afterthought in efforts to tackle the prison overcrowding crisis - they should be the Government’s priority. Having already shown extraordinary perseverance and resilience to endure painfully long waits for justice, many will feel shocked and frightened to learn that offenders may now be released months or even years earlier than expected.

‌



"It is completely unacceptable that, for the vast majority, there is no way to even find out if or how they are affected. No victim should be left in the dark. Every single person affected by these changes should be able to quickly and easily find out how their offender's sentence has changed and what it means for them.”

View 2 Images Justice Secretary David Lammy faces calls to extend victims' right to know about early release (Image: Getty Images)

Currently those eligible for the Victim Contact Scheme (VCS) are able to find out if an offender's sentence has changed. This is open to victims of violent and sexual offences where the sentence is a year or more behind bars. However Ministry of Justice (MOJ) stats show 58% of criminals given an immediate jail term are sentenced to less than a year.

‌



Inability to find out about early release could undermine faith in the justice system, the charity warns. It has called on the government to ensure all victims are able to find out if a sentence has changed, and what it means for them.

The Ministry of Justice said early release has been introduced to stop prisons running out of space by November. It said those who do qualify for early release will face tough restrictions on their movements, such as tagging, and probation services are being ramped up.

Under new rules eligible prisoners can be released after serving 33% of their sentence if they meet conditions. The earliest release date for inmates serving over four years for violent or sexual offences, has been brought forward to 50%.

‌



A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said “This government is fixing the prison crisis it inherited – building 14,000 more prison places and reforming sentencing so we can always lock up dangerous criminals. Without this decisive action, prisons will run out of space entirely as early as November and we will be unable to lock up serious offenders at all.

“Public safety and supporting victims is our top priority. Offenders who a judge has deemed the most dangerous are automatically blocked from early release, and prisoners who behave badly while behind bars face being locked up for longer.

“Anyone who is released faces tough rules such as restrictions on their movements, tagging, being banned from attending public events, pubs and clubs, backed by our record £700m investment into probation and 1,300 extra probation officers.”

Article continues below

Under current rules victims who opt into the Victim Contact Scheme will be notified of an offender's release. When the Tories were in power extended notice was not given under previous release schemes.

The government said supervision of released inmates can be more intense than ever, and those who break rules will be immediately returned to prison.

Ministers are understood to be committed to delivering a service that provides victims with a clear route to request information about an offender's release. Meetings have been held with victim support organisations recently, and the government has pledged to continue working with them.

News.title: Prince Harry live: Duke jokes with Alison Hammond as Meghan and kids miss event
News.content:
Prince Harry is spending the day at a one-year to go celebration for his Invictus Games in Birmingham today - but he will not be joined by wife Meghan Markle as originally planned

Prince Harry has arrived at a huge event for his Invictus Games today - where he has tried his hand at numerous sports and chatted with Invictus officials and royal fans.

The Duke of Sussex also appeared on This Morning, as he spoke with Alison Hammond - who has a special interest in the 2027 Games due to her Birmingham heritage - about the impact the Invictus Games has around the world.

During their conversation, Harry revealed that his children, Archie and Lilibet, love the charismatic presenter on the Great British Bake Off, to which Alison was elated. Harry went on to say the UK Bake Off is "far better" than the US version.

Elsewhere, Harry and Alison took part in a Laser Run game, which involves running around an indoor track and shooting at targets with laser pistols.

Meghan Markle and the couple’s children are understood to be in the UK, but the Duchess was unable to attend today’s event due to security concerns caused by the family being refused police protection. The family are believed to be staying at the Spencer family home of Althorp.

The Duchess coming to the UK could pave the way for King Charles to have an emotional reunion with his grandchildren; seven-year-old Archie and Lilibet, five, whom he hasn't seen since 2022. That occasion — the late Queen Elizabeth II’s Platinum Jubilee — remains the only time Charles has met Lilibet.

The Mirror exclusively reported this week the monarch, 77, has instructed senior aides to engage in ongoing talks with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, to secure time in his busy diary around his public duties, and this looks set now to be Friday or Saturday in London.

News.title: Spain wildfires live: 'Several Brit tourists' dead in Almeria as bodies found in car
News.content:
Twelve people have been killed in a wildfire in Los Gallardos, Almería, Spain - at least four of the dead are thought to be British and were found in a burnt out car

FOUR Brits 'feared DEAD in Spain' after burnt out car found in WILDFIRE in Los Gallardos

Several Brits are feared to have died in a wildfire in Spain which has claimed 12 lives.

Officials said four people found dead in a burned out car in Los Gallardos, Almería are believed to be British. There are also fears that Brits could be among a group of people found dead while trying to escape the flames on foot.

Witnesses say the wildfire was caused by a downed power line, although authorities have not confirmed the cause. Around 150 firefighters have been deployed to tackle the fire in a hamlet called Bedar. It comes as Europe continues to battle a raging 40C heatwave.
